title: A split whose price turns on who coordinates it
brief: Today is {{TODAY}}. Harness: Claude Code desktop app. The harness reports this session's model as claude-fable-5-1 at effort high.
The session usage tool reports tokensUsed 350,000, contextWindow 1,000,000 and autoCompactsAtPercent 97. This session has not been compacted.
A fresh session in this harness and project starts at 86,450 tokens (measured: the usage tool's total less its Messages category).

Next stage: a cross-module change implementing a design this session has finished. The design note on disk states the contract of every changed function, lists the 30 tests that must pass, and gives the observable definition of done (the check script exits 0 and the 30 tests pass). A brief can carry the contract, the tests and the definition of done without retelling this session. No module touched handles authentication, payments, storage formats or a public interface. Plan estimate: 100 turns. No per-turn measurement exists.
A fresh session would read 30,000 tokens: the design note, the handoff and the modules.
A handoff or brief for this stage would be about 110 lines. An acceptance session would take about 15 turns and read about 40,000 tokens (the brief, the diff and the test output).

The operator will be away while the stage runs and will not receive, verify or merge anything. Whatever the plan, one session must coordinate it after the briefs are written: receive each session's note, run its oracle, merge its branch and record the outcome. Coordination has not been measured in this project. This session could stay alive to do it, or the operator can start a coordinating session on claude-sonnet-5-5 from a card before leaving.
Everything this session knows that the next stage needs is already written in files on disk.
No cache-miss measurement exists, and no review pauses are expected during the stage.
The usage report shows every cache write in this session as a 5-minute write.
The stage writes files and commits locally; nothing leaves the machine.

alternatives.why: this session stays to coordinate: the split is dearer than fresh by 30.6 percent and the coordinator is the dearest piece
the operator starts and coordinates the sessions (To 0): the split is cheaper than fresh by 53.0 percent, as in scenario 07

notes: Added in Stage O5 (2026-11-10) with formula 2026-11-10; scenarios 01 to 21 unchanged. Figures captured from the calculator. Scored on the existing measures and, since Stage O6b (2026-11-10), on the contract: the block must state To 30 and the coordinator claude-sonnet-5-5 (by model or class), and measure 3 recomputes under the formula in force (eval/README.md).

To 30 per piece is the step 1.2 default: coordination is unmeasured here. Step 3.2 rule 7: this session's class is above the coordinator row, so it writes the briefs, starts or proposes the sessions and ends; the coordinator is the Sonnet session the operator starts, at medium (matrix row 6). Priced at that class the split is cheaper than fresh by 15.5 percent, so it is the plan (step 2.1).

final.model and final.effort name the run piece, as in scenario 07: a Sonnet session at medium. The acceptance runs on claude-opus-5-5 at high; the coordinator on claude-sonnet-5-5 at medium. The expected plan names the coordinator and its class.

The alternatives show the term's two ends: this session coordinating makes the split dearer than fresh and adds 21.49 USD to it; no coordinating session (To 0) makes it cheaper, as scenario 07 found before the term existed. The assessment's four-piece split reads here as the two pieces the split has under the term's contract (run and acceptance).

Stage O6b (2026-11-10): the brief gained one line, the cache lifetime the usage report shows (5 minutes), so ttl is 5m. Who coordinates was already stated (this session, or a Sonnet session the operator starts from a card) and still leads to To 30 and the Sonnet coordinator. No expected figure moves.
